criteria.name: Correct identity and source-backed footprint
evidence: Raw Purdue GIS record FID 758 names Sigma Nu / SOSN at 1301 Tower Dr; the independent Beta Zeta newsletter photo visibly shows the 1301 address plaque.
GIS polygon has 10 vertices. Builder's saved-file report claims symmetric base-ring vertex error 0.00003749 m; I could not independently recompute this from Blender geometry.

Visual comparison of the current preview and source photo supports a broad match in building identity and massing footprint, with the GIS polygon treated as a roof/building proxy rather than measured wall line.
uncertainty: No surveyed wall footprint; roof edge offset is unknown.

criteria.name: Position, orientation, and scale/dimensions
evidence: The saved evidence records the repository's approximate EPSG:4326-to-campus conversion and provides raw GIS and OSM snapshots.

Preview geometry is consistent with the GIS polygon; the reopen report states 0.00003749 m ring error and world bounds, but those Blender values remain builder-reported because a new Blender reopen was unavailable.

OSM Tower Drive context supports the chosen north/northwest-facing edge only indirectly; source register itself correctly calls the facade bearing an inference (Road geometry is volunteered mapping and does not directly measure the building facade bearing; the front selection remains an inference.).
uncertainty: No independent survey/CRS check. The photo is not georeferenced, so front-bearing assignment is still inferred.

criteria.name: Evidence-backed height, floors, and roof form
evidence: The image supports a low, broad, multi-level appearance but supplies no known scale or elevation; the model's 7.2 m wall and 7.45 m top values are estimates.
The GIS NUM_LEVELS=1 and Extrution=44 metadata are undocumented and do not verify storey count or height.
The preview shows a low flat cap; the provided photos do not establish its form or dimensions.
uncertainty: Actual story count, wall height, roof profile, and overall height remain unverified.

criteria.name: Facade, entrances, and distinctive architecture
evidence: Fall 2019 newsletter photograph of the address plaque provides direct facade imagery. Its front photo supports brickwork, a broad central entrance zone with light trim, and multiple front openings; the lower side photo supports a projecting bay and red-brick side wall.

The current preview uses subdued red-brown upper brick, a light lower band, two main facade windows, a central opening/canopy, and a restrained side bay. These are broad, defensible generalizations from the visible image.

Newsletter record explicitly disclaims exact elevations and measurements: The printed newsletter raster is perspective-distorted and partly occluded; it does not establish exact dimensions, floor elevations, roof silhouette, or unseen elevations. The pictured building is not georeferenced to a particular GIS edge.
uncertainty: Exact window count/spacing, sill/lintel details, story split, trim material, and unseen elevations cannot be confirmed; facade bearing is not tied to photo by georeferencing.

criteria.name: Modular export, portability, and complete evidence
evidence: Expected .blend, builder script, preview, raw GIS/newsletter/OSM snapshots, and source register are present.

Builder's reopen record reports expected scene Building_massing_house_301841330_f58ae87, export collection Asset_massing_house_301841330_f58ae87, 24 mesh objects, no modifiers or relative dependencies; these claims could not be independently confirmed with Blender in this review.
Saved validation records geometry bounds and uncertainty; asset appears self-contained from source and render evidence.
uncertainty: Independent load of the final .blend and inspection of collection membership, world matrices, dependencies, and evaluated meshes could not be performed in this environment.

builder_reopen_record.facade_bearing: North/northwest-facing long GIS edge toward Tower Drive, bearing inferred from OSM road context; image is not georeferenced.
builder_reopen_record.visual_review: Reopened and inspected preview; exact GIS shell, two-level light base/red brick upper wall, dark low roof cap, front entry, two main-elevation windows and one restrained side bay are present.

independent_fresh_reopen.reason: Blender connector reported it could not connect to Blender; no local blender.exe or bpy Python module was available.

findings: Score is below the 8/10 threshold. The current iteration improves the previously criticized facade generalization: broad brick/light-masonry contrast and the entrance/bay now align with visible newsletter imagery, with fewer unsupported openings.

Most limiting criterion is height/floors/roof (0.6/2): current sources do not establish story count, heights, or roof silhouette. Find measured elevation/assessor imagery with an exact parcel match, or continue to mark these as provisional estimates.

Independent Blender reopen was unavailable, so all numerical mesh/export properties from reopen_validation.json are reported builder evidence, not independently reproduced checks. A reviewer with Blender access should freshly load the exact saved asset before sign-off.
The GIS ring is an excellent reported plan-shape match but remains a building/roof polygon proxy; facade bearing is contextual inference only.
